from_notes: INS Sarvekshak: hydrographic survey ship – first Indian Navy ship to install a solar power system (Green Initiative, February 2017); 18 flexible panels of 300 W each.
x: INS Sarvekshak, a hydrographic survey ship of the Southern Naval Command, was the first Indian Navy ship to install a solar power system under the Navy's Green Initiative (February 2017): 18 flexible 300-W panels, about 5.4 kW. Vikramaditya (carrier), Virat (decommissioned carrier) and Kalvari (submarine) were not part of this project.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INS_Sarvekshak ('the 1st ship of Indian Navy ever to deploy solar power', 2017; 300-W panels, 5.4 kW, citing Economic Times 'INS Sarvekshak goes green; instals solar power system')
evidence: Local library (NextGen, Rocket CA 2026 Part 01-04, Praveen CA-360): no line on INS Sarvekshak

Web search results (indiannavy.nic.in/node/16512 'Green Initiative Installation of Solar Panel Onboard INS Sarvekshak'; Business Standard/PTI 12 Feb 2017: 18 flexible panels of 300 W) – pages not opened (403/503), summaries only

from_notes: Varuna-2004 – French nuclear carrier Charles De Gaulle (crew ~1,950).
x: Charles De Gaulle's complement is about 1,350 ship's company plus about 600 in the air wing – roughly 1,950 in all, the figure reported for Varuna-2004 (April 2004). 2,000 is only a rounded figure, and 156 and 105 are far too small for a nuclear-powered carrier.
evidence: Local library (NextGen, Rocket CA 2026 Part 01-04, Praveen CA-360): no Varuna-2004 crew figure; Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.149 / Part 02 p.123 list only Varuna-2026

Web search: March 2004 report quoting the carrier's captain Xavier Magne – about 1,900 persons on board (globalsecurity.org, page not opened, 403); no page found giving 1,950 directly – 1,950 = 1,350 + 600 from Wikipedia

x: Varuna-2026, the 24th edition, was held at Toulon, France (began 22 September, concluded 28 September) with INS Trishul. The India–France naval exercise was initiated in 1993 (not 1983) and named Varuna in 2001.
source: manoramayearbook.in/current-affairs/india/2026/10/03/india-france-varuna-naval-exercise.html ('Initiated in 1993, the exercise was renamed Varuna in 2001'; 24th edition concluded in Toulon on 28 September); Rocket CA 2026 Part 02 p.123 (Varuna-2026, Toulon Naval Base, 24th)
evidence: Praveen CA-360 Sep 2026 magazine (src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-09-magazine.txt) says 'began in 1983' – contradicted by the Navy-sourced reports of 1993
Web search: Business Standard / Deccan Herald on the 21st edition (2023): 'initiated in 1993, and christened Varuna in 2001' (summaries)
